# The Rationalist Accuses Us of Denying Truth

When the pragmatist undertakes to show in detail just WHY we must defer, the rationalist is unable to recognize the concretes from which his own abstraction is taken.[^1] He accuses us,[^2] Messrs.[^3] Dewey, Schiller and their allies,[^4] of DENYING truth; whereas we have only sought to trace exactly why people follow it and always ought to follow it.[^5]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "When the pragmatist undertakes to show in detail just WHY we must defer, the rationalist is unable to recognize the concretes from which his own abstraction is taken."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "He accuses us"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Messrs."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth]] "Dewey, Schiller and their allies"
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "of DENYING truth; whereas we have only sought to trace exactly why people follow it and always ought to follow it."
